rows.sub: In a green valley in central Vietnam, red brick towers rise out of the jungle. Some of them are more than a thousand years old.
rows.say: In a green valley in central Vietnam, red brick towers rise out of the jungle. Some of them are more than a thousand years old.

rows.sub: The people who built them ruled parts of this coast for more than a thousand years. Their kingdom was called Champa.
rows.say: The people who built them ruled parts of this coast for more than a thousand years. Their kingdom was called Chahm-pah.

rows.sub: It was a sea power that traded with China and sacked a Vietnamese capital. Its name even lived on in China, as the name of a rice.
rows.say: It was a sea power that traded with China and sacked a Vietnamese capital. Its name even lived on in China, as the name of a rice.

rows.sub: Today, Champa has no capital and no state. But its people are still here.
rows.say: Today, Chahm-pah has no capital and no state. But its people are still here.

rows.sub: This is the story of how Champa rose, how it ended, and what remains.
rows.say: This is the story of how Chahm-pah rose, how it ended, and what remains.

rows.sub: The Cham spoke an Austronesian language. Its closest relatives are not Vietnamese or Khmer, but languages like Acehnese and Malay, spoken across the sea.
rows.say: The Chahm spoke an Austronesian language. Its closest relatives are not Vietnamese or Khmer, but languages like Ah-chay-neez and Malay, spoken across the sea.

rows.sub: Chinese histories describe a kingdom on this coast called Linyi, from roughly the second or third century CE. Whether Linyi was Champa itself is still debated.
rows.say: Chinese histories describe a kingdom on this coast called Lin-yee, from roughly the second or third century C E. Whether Lin-yee was Chahm-pah itself is still debated.

rows.sub: Champa was not always a single unified state. Some historians describe several regional centers along the coast, sometimes united and sometimes rivals.
rows.say: Chahm-pah was not always a single unified state. Some historians describe several regional centers along the coast, sometimes united and sometimes rivals.

rows.sub: Indrapura in the north. Vijaya. Kauthara. And Panduranga, in the dry far south.
rows.say: Indra-poora in the north. Vee-jaya. Kow-tah-rah. And Pahn-doo-rahng-gah, in the dry far south.

rows.sub: These centers grew at river mouths, facing the sea. Chinese records describe Cham traders bringing ivory, rhinoceros horn and fragrant aloeswood.
rows.say: These centers grew at river mouths, facing the sea. Chinese records describe Chahm traders bringing ivory, rhinoceros horn and fragrant aloeswood.

rows.sub: Their harbors lay along sea routes linking China and the Indian Ocean. Ships from both worlds stopped on this coast.
rows.say: Their harbors lay along sea routes linking China and the Indian Ocean. Ships from both worlds stopped on this coast.

rows.sub: Cham rulers built in fired red brick, decorated with carved sandstone. Their temple towers still stand along the coast.
rows.say: Chahm rulers built in fired red brick, decorated with carved sandstone. Their temple towers still stand along the coast.

rows.sub: Many were dedicated to Shiva, a Hindu god. At Mỹ Sơn, inscriptions honor Bhadreśvara, a form of Shiva named after an early king, Bhadravarman.
rows.say: Many were dedicated to Shiva, a Hindu god. At Mee Sun, inscriptions honor Bhad-raysh-vara, a form of Shiva named after an early king, Bhadra-varman.

rows.sub: But Champa was not only Hindu. In the ninth century, a large Buddhist monastery was established at Đồng Dương.
rows.say: But Chahm-pah was not only Hindu. In the ninth century, a large Buddhist monastery was established at Dong Zuong.

rows.sub: Inscriptions were written in Sanskrit, the classical language of India, and in Old Cham, the language of the Cham.
rows.say: Inscriptions were written in Sanskrit, the classical language of India, and in Old Chahm, the language of the Chahm.

rows.sub: One Old Cham stone, from Đông Yên Châu, is often described as one of the oldest known texts in any Austronesian language. Its exact date is still studied.
rows.say: One Old Chahm stone, from Dong Yen Chow, is often described as one of the oldest known texts in any Austronesian language. Its exact date is still studied.

rows.sub: Further south, at Kauthara, the Cham worshipped a goddess at the towers of Po Nagar. We will come back to her.
rows.say: Further south, at Kow-tah-rah, the Chahm worshipped a goddess at the towers of Poh Nah-gar. We will come back to her.

rows.sub: Mỹ Sơn is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Some of its towers were damaged during the Vietnam War.
rows.say: Mee Sun is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Some of its towers were damaged during the Vietnam War.

rows.sub: Champa's name traveled further than its ships. In Song China, farmers grew a rice known as Champa rice.
rows.say: Chahm-pah's name traveled further than its ships. In Song China, farmers grew a rice known as Chahm-pah rice.

rows.sub: Song records describe Champa rice as a variety that ripened early and could survive with less water.
rows.say: Song records describe Chahm-pah rice as a variety that ripened early and could survive with less water.

rows.sub: Song records, as discussed by historian Ho Ping-ti, say that in 1012 Emperor Zhenzong ordered thirty thousand bushels of seed from Fujian to be shared out in the Yangzi and Huai regions.
rows.say: Song records, as discussed by historian Ho Ping-tee, say that in ten twelve Emperor Jen-zong ordered thirty thousand bushels of seed from Foo-jen to be shared out in the Yahng-zuh and Huai regions.

rows.sub: The rice had probably reached southern China earlier, by sea. Ho argued it helped China grow far more food. Others think its effect was slower and more local.
rows.say: The rice had probably reached southern China earlier, by sea. Ho argued it helped China grow far more food. Others think its effect was slower and more local.

rows.sub: Where did it come from first? A 2011 genetic study links these varieties to a rice group from South Asia. Champa may have been one stop on its journey, but the name stuck: Champa rice.
rows.say: Where did it come from first? A 2011 genetic study links these varieties to a rice group from South Asia. Chahm-pah may have been one stop on its journey, but the name stuck: Chahm-pah rice.

rows.sub: Champa was also a military power, and it fought neighbors on both sides.
rows.say: Chahm-pah was also a military power, and it fought neighbors on both sides.

rows.sub: To the west lay the Khmer empire of Angkor. In the conventional account, a Cham force attacked Angkor in 1177. Historian Michael Vickery doubts parts of that story.
rows.say: To the west lay the Khmer empire of Angkor. In the conventional account, a Chahm force attacked Angkor in eleven seventy-seven. Historian Michael Vickery doubts parts of that story.

rows.sub: Khmer forces under Jayavarman the Seventh later campaigned in parts of Champa.
rows.say: Khmer forces under Jaya-varman the Seventh later campaigned in parts of Chahm-pah.

rows.sub: To the north lay Đại Việt, the Vietnamese kingdom of the Red River. Here too, wars ran both ways.
rows.say: To the north lay Dye Vee-et, the Vietnamese kingdom of the Red River. Here too, wars ran both ways.

rows.sub: Cham inscriptions, Vietnamese chronicles and Chinese records each tell these wars from their own side.
rows.say: Chahm inscriptions, Vietnamese chronicles and Chinese records each tell these wars from their own side.

rows.sub: In 1069, Đại Việt's king Lý Thánh Tông captured the Cham king. Vietnamese chronicles say three northern districts were given up for his release.
rows.say: In ten sixty-nine, Dye Vee-et's king Lee Tahn Tong captured the Chahm king. Vietnamese chronicles say three northern districts were given up for his release.
rows.src: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (1479)

rows.sub: In 1306, a Cham king married a Vietnamese princess, Huyền Trân. In the Vietnamese chronicles, two more districts passed to Đại Việt with the marriage.
rows.say: In thirteen oh-six, a Chahm king married a Vietnamese princess, Hwen Chun. In the Vietnamese chronicles, two more districts passed to Dye Vee-et with the marriage.

rows.sub: Then the tide turned. In the late fourteenth century, a Cham king the Vietnamese called Chế Bồng Nga led attack after attack to the north.
rows.say: Then the tide turned. In the late fourteenth century, a Chahm king the Vietnamese called Cheh Bong Ngah led attack after attack to the north.

rows.sub: In 1371, Cham forces sacked Thăng Long, the capital of Đại Việt.
rows.say: In thirteen seventy-one, Chahm forces sacked Tahng Long, the capital of Dye Vee-et.

rows.sub: His campaigns went on for almost twenty years, until he was killed in battle in 1390. His real Cham name is not known.
rows.say: His campaigns went on for almost twenty years, until he was killed in battle in thirteen ninety. His real Chahm name is not known.

rows.sub: After his death, the balance of power slowly turned against Champa.
rows.say: After his death, the balance of power slowly turned against Chahm-pah.

rows.sub: In 1471, Đại Việt's emperor Lê Thánh Tông led a large army south against Vijaya, the Cham capital.
rows.say: In fourteen seventy-one, Dye Vee-et's emperor Lay Tahn Tong led a large army south against Vee-jaya, the Chahm capital.

rows.sub: The city fell. The Cham king, called Trà Toàn in Vietnamese records, was captured with his family.
rows.say: The city fell. The Chahm king, called Chah Twahn in Vietnamese records, was captured with his family.

rows.sub: Vijaya became a major Cham capital around the eleventh century. Cham towers still stand near the city of Quy Nhơn.
rows.say: Vee-jaya became a major Chahm capital around the eleventh century. Chahm towers still stand near the city of Kwee Nyun.

rows.sub: How many died? The sources do not agree. The Vietnamese court chronicle claims over 40,000 killed and over 30,000 captured. Those are its own figures, not a settled count.
rows.say: How many died? The sources do not agree. The Vietnamese court chronicle claims over forty thousand killed and over thirty thousand captured. Those are its own figures, not a settled count.
rows.src: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư, cited in Kiernan 2009

rows.sub: The Ming history, written in China, records the king and more than fifty of his relatives taken away.
rows.say: The Ming history, written in China, records the king and more than fifty of his relatives taken away.

rows.sub: The northern lands of Vijaya became part of Đại Việt. Further south, smaller Cham kingdoms survived.
rows.say: The northern lands of Vee-jaya became part of Dye Vee-et. Further south, smaller Chahm kingdoms survived.

rows.sub: A Cham envoy told the Ming court that Annam had sacked and occupied their country.
rows.say: A Chahm envoy told the Ming court that Annam had sacked and occupied their country.

rows.sub: According to Ming records, the court sent orders to Annam. Vijaya was never returned to Cham rule.
rows.say: According to Ming records, the court sent orders to Annam. Vee-jaya was never returned to Chahm rule.

rows.sub: For the Cham, the heartland of their northern kingdoms was gone.
rows.say: For the Chahm, the heartland of their northern kingdoms was gone.

rows.sub: After 1471, Champa lived on in the south, smaller with each century.
rows.say: After fourteen seventy-one, Chahm-pah lived on in the south, smaller with each century.

rows.sub: The Nguyễn lords, who ruled southern Đại Việt, moved their frontier step by step: Phú Yên around 1611, Kauthara in 1653.
rows.say: The Nwin lords, who ruled southern Dye Vee-et, moved their frontier step by step: Foo Yen around sixteen eleven, Kow-tah-rah in sixteen fifty-three.

rows.sub: In the 1690s they took Panduranga, the last Cham principality. After resistance, they let a Cham ruler govern it again, under Nguyễn authority.
rows.say: In the sixteen-nineties they took Pahn-doo-rahng-gah, the last Chahm principality. After resistance, they let a Chahm ruler govern it again, under Nwin authority.

rows.sub: Vietnamese settlement spread into lands that had been Cham territory.
rows.say: Vietnamese settlement spread into lands that had been Chahm territory.

rows.sub: For more than a century, Panduranga kept Cham rulers, and its court kept records in the Cham script.
rows.say: For more than a century, Pahn-doo-rahng-gah kept Chahm rulers, and its court kept records in the Chahm script.

rows.sub: In 1832, Emperor Minh Mạng ended that arrangement and brought Panduranga under direct rule, as a province of Vietnam.
rows.say: In eighteen thirty-two, Emperor Min Mahng ended that arrangement and brought Pahn-doo-rahng-gah under direct rule, as a province of Vietnam.

rows.sub: Revolts followed, and were put down by 1835. Cham poems from those years recorded the new rules, and how they changed Cham life.
rows.say: Revolts followed, and were put down by eighteen thirty-five. Chahm poems from those years recorded the new rules, and how they changed Chahm life.

rows.sub: A kingdom that had faced the sea for more than a thousand years ended as a state.
rows.say: A kingdom that had faced the sea for more than a thousand years ended as a state.

rows.sub: It is tempting to ask what might have been. But history has no "if". It has only what happened, and what remains.
rows.say: It is tempting to ask what might have been. But history has no "if". It has only what happened, and what remains.

rows.sub: And what remains is a people. Vietnam's 2019 census counted about 179,000 Cham, and Cham communities also live in Cambodia.
rows.say: And what remains is a people. Vietnam's twenty nineteen census counted about a hundred and seventy-nine thousand Chahm, and Chahm communities also live in Cambodia.

rows.sub: Some follow a Hindu-based tradition, some Bani, some Sunni Islam. Their own script, Akhar Thrah, is still taught in some village schools.
rows.say: Some follow a Hindu-based tradition, some Bah-nee, some Sunni Islam. Their own script, Ah-kar Trah, is still taught in some village schools.

rows.sub: Each year, Cham communities celebrate Katê at towers such as Po Klong Garai. Vietnam recognized the festival as national intangible heritage in 2017.
rows.say: Each year, Chahm communities celebrate Kah-tay at towers such as Poh Klong Gah-rye. Vietnam recognized the festival as national intangible heritage in 2017.

rows.sub: Cham women still shape pottery by hand, walking around the clay instead of turning a wheel. UNESCO listed their craft in 2022.
rows.say: Chahm women still shape pottery by hand, walking around the clay instead of turning a wheel. UNESCO listed their craft in 2022.

rows.sub: At Po Nagar, Cham worshippers honor the goddess Po Ina Nagar. Vietnamese pilgrims honor her too, as Thiên Y A Na, in the same towers.
rows.say: At Poh Nah-gar, Chahm worshippers honor the goddess Poh Ee-nah Nah-gar. Vietnamese pilgrims honor her too, as Tee-en Ee Ah Nah, in the same towers.

rows.sub: And in Cham homes, festival tables still carry their own dishes, like the ginger cakes offered to the ancestors.
rows.say: And in Chahm homes, festival tables still carry their own dishes, like the ginger cakes offered to the ancestors.

rows.sub: The kingdom ended. Its people, its gods and its towers did not.
rows.say: The kingdom ended. Its people, its gods and its towers did not.

rows.sub: What did you know about Champa before this video? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to Rice and Empires.
rows.say: What did you know about Chahm-pah before this video? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to Rice and Empires.

tl.caption: Cham kings on the coast, from the first inscriptions (dates debated) to 1832
